title: NAMES, CHANGES, AND A SETTLED PEOPLE

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: And the Reubenites rebuilt Heshbon, Elealeh and Kiriathaim, as well as Nebo and Baal Meon (these names were changed) and Sibmah. They gave names to the cities they rebuilt. The descendants of Makir son of Manasseh went to Gilead, captured it and drove out the Amorites who were there. So Moses gave Gilead to the Makirites, the descendants of Manasseh, and they settled there. Jair, a descendant of Manasseh, captured its settlements and called them Havvoth Jair. And Nobah captured Kenath and its surrounding settlements and named it Nobah after himself. - Num 32:37-42 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The chapter closes with a list of cities rebuilt, captured, and renamed. Some of the old pagan names — like those tied to Baal — were changed, a quiet but meaningful act. As God's people took possession of the land, they did not simply move into the old ways; they marked the places with new names, signalling a new belonging. What had been dedicated to false gods was being reclaimed.

There is a gentle picture of transformation here. When God takes hold of a life, things get renamed. Old identities tied to sin and idolatry are left behind, and something new is written over them. Throughout Scripture, God gives new names to mark new beginnings — Abram became Abraham, Jacob became Israel, Simon became Peter. A new name speaks of a new belonging and a new future.

This is exactly what God does for us in Christ. The old has gone; the new has come (2 Cor 5:17). We are no longer defined by our former way of life, by our failures, or by the idols we once served. We belong to God now, and He writes His own name over us. One day He promises to give His people a new name, known fully in His presence (Rev 2:17).

As this chapter of settling and renaming ends, let it remind you: in Christ, you have a new name and a new home. The territory of your life, once claimed by other things, now belongs to the Lord. Live in the freedom of that new belonging.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What "old names" or identities has Christ freed you from?
2. Are there areas of your life still marked by old ways that need reclaiming for God?
3. How does belonging to God give you a new sense of identity and home?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that in Christ I am made new and given a new belonging. Reclaim every part of my life for Yourself, and help me to live in the freedom of my new identity in You. Amen.
